Cauda Equina Syndrome: The patient presents with progressively worsening urinary symptoms, fecal incontinence, and reduced anal tone, which are consistent with cauda equina syndrome. The MRI finding of a lesion distal to the conus causing peripheral displacement of the cauda equina roots at L1/2 level further supports this diagnosis.
Spinal Cord Compression: The patient's symptoms of urinary and fecal incontinence, along with the MRI finding of a lesion compressing the spinal cord, are consistent with spinal cord compression. This diagnosis is also supported by the patient's newly developed mild lower limb numbness and brisker reflex in the right knee.
